answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create urgency, but the 94% volume utilization and assembly line dependency preclude switching primary vendors or deferring. memory_c4 demonstrated that renegotiation with the incumbent recovered real margin through benchmarking; memory_c2 showed the low-cost alternative is unreliable for critical lines (three SLA misses in four quarters). Verifying both will confirm whether aggressive renegotiation can bridge the cost gap and whether the incumbent has further concessions available. memory_c6 showed multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing; memory_c1 confirmed renewal stability; memory_c3 established second-source value for constraints. A standard negotiation experiment targets the cost reduction without disrupting delivery. If renegotiation fails, we revisit add_second_source or defer_decision in the next cycle. This approach preserves budget flexibility and avoids sole-vendor risk while addressing the immediate deadline.
